seoTitle: How to Host a Website on Google Workspace (Google Sites)
metaDescription: Learn how to host your website using Google Sites within Google Workspace in 2026, starting from a blank page or a ready-made template.
intro: Google Sites gives Workspace users a straightforward way to build and host a website without needing separate hosting or coding skills, and the whole thing starts from the same account you already use for Gmail and Drive. This guide covers signing into that account, landing on the Sites start screen, and choosing between a blank page and a template depending on how much design work you want to do yourself.

steps.heading: Sign in to your Google Workspace account
steps.body: Go to your Workspace login and enter the credentials for the account tied to your organization's domain — a business account looks the same as a personal Gmail login, just with your own domain in place of gmail.com. If you're signed into multiple Google accounts on the same browser, double-check which one you're entering a password for, since Sites created under the wrong account won't inherit your Workspace's storage, sharing permissions, or custom domain settings.

image.caption: The Google sign-in screen prompting for a password on a Workspace account tied to a custom domain.

steps.heading: Open Google Sites from your Workspace apps
steps.body: Once you're signed in, open the Google apps grid (the nine-dot icon) from any Google service and look for Sites, or go directly to sites.google.com. Because it's a native Workspace app, anything you build here is stored in the same Drive as your documents and spreadsheets, and it inherits your organization's sharing defaults automatically — useful if multiple people on your team need editing access.

steps.heading: Choose blank or start from a template
steps.body: The Sites home screen opens on "Start a new site," with a Blank site tile marked by a colored plus icon sitting first in a row of starting points. Clicking Blank site drops you straight into an empty canvas with no pre-built sections, which is the right call if you want full control over layout from page one. The tiles next to it are template starting points — pre-arranged pages and sections you customize instead of building from nothing, which saves time if you'd rather adjust an existing layout than design one yourself.

image.caption: The "Start a new site" screen, with Blank site as the first option in a row of starting points you can build from.

steps.heading: Build out your pages
steps.body: Whichever starting point you pick, the Sites editor works the same way: a right-hand panel for adding text boxes, images, embeds, and layout blocks, and a Pages tab for adding new pages and arranging them into your site's navigation. Keep the number of top-level pages manageable — a visitor should be able to see your whole site's structure in the navigation bar without scrolling through a long dropdown, so group related content under a single page with sections rather than creating a new page for every topic.

steps.heading: Preview before you publish
steps.body: Use the preview button in the editor's top bar to see the site as a visitor would, including how it collapses down for mobile screens. This is worth doing before every publish, not just the first one — a layout that looks fine on your wide editor window can crowd or overlap on a phone, and catching that in preview costs nothing compared to catching it after a visitor complains.

steps.heading: Publish and set your web address
steps.body: When you're ready, click Publish in the top-right corner. By default your site gets a Google-hosted address ending in sites.google.com, but if you want it to appear under your own domain, you can connect a custom domain from the site's settings — this typically involves adding a verification record through your domain registrar, so budget a little time for DNS changes to take effect before the custom address starts working.

faq.question: Is Google Sites free with Google Workspace?
faq.answer: Google Sites is included with most Google Workspace plans at no extra cost, though storage for your site's images and files draws from your overall Workspace storage allowance.

faq.question: Can I use my own domain with a Google Sites website?
faq.answer: Yes, you can connect a custom domain you own to your Google Sites page instead of using the default sites.google.com address, through a verification step in the site's settings.

faq.question: Is it better to start with a blank site or a template?
faq.answer: Templates save time and offer a pre-arranged layout you customize, while a blank site is better if you want complete control over the structure from the very first page.

faq.question: Can multiple people in my organization edit the same site?
faq.answer: Yes, since Sites is a native Workspace app, it inherits your organization's sharing defaults, so teammates with the right permissions can edit the site together like any shared Drive file.

faq.question: Where do I go to start a new site?
faq.answer: Sign into your Workspace account, open Sites from the Google apps grid or sites.google.com, and choose Blank site or a template from the "Start a new site" screen.
